sections.h2: Which office values and bills property in Robeson County?
sections.html:
One department does both jobs. The Robeson County Tax Administrator serves as assessor and collector, handling the listing and valuation of real property, personal property and motor vehicles, the collection of taxes, land records and mapping, and countywide reappraisal.

It has three divisions. Assessment covers real property, reappraisal, personal property, individual and business listings, and motor vehicles. Collections has a customer service section and a delinquent collections section. Land Records and GIS keeps the maps and addresses.

The Lumberton office answers at 910-671-3060. The county's online tools let you look up real and personal property bills and search public land records, and the phone payment line (1-866-249-0705) carries a convenience fee. Have the parcel number, owner name or bill in hand before you search.

sections.h2: When did Robeson County last reappraise real estate?
sections.html:
The most recent reappraisal took effect January 1, 2024. State law calls for one at least every eight years, and the county's page says the commissioners have considered a four-year cycle to narrow gaps between fast and slow neighborhoods.

About 560 appraisal neighborhoods organize the work. Appraisers study cost, sales and income data and build a schedule of values that the Board of Commissioners adopts. Family sales, gifts, trades and deals between related companies are set aside as non-market transfers, and the county notes that a seller under pressure may accept less than market value, so a single sale price does not set the assessment.

Between reappraisals, values move only for new construction, demolition, remodeling, a zoning change or a correction of an error. Real property is listed permanently, which means no yearly listing unless you built, tore down, or lost a program benefit.

sections.h2: What is the Robeson County tax calendar from bill to penalty?
sections.html:
Robeson mails real and personal property bills each August. They fall due September 1, though interest waits until after January 5. A 2 percent charge arrives January 6, then the county adds three-fourths of a percent on the first of each following month.

Robeson County real and personal property billing sequence from the county tax page
StepTiming
Bills mailedAugust
DueSeptember 1
Last day without interestJanuary 5
First interest charge2 percent, January 6
Added monthlyThree-fourths of 1 percent
Newspaper advertisingMarch, with a fee added to the bill

The state collection statute, G.S. 105-360, uses the same due date and interest steps. Collection can start once a bill is delinquent, using wage garnishment, bank attachment, foreclosure, income tax refund set-off or levies on rents.

sections.h2: How must Robeson County residents list boats, mobile homes and business equipment?
sections.html:
Listing is annual, with a January 31 deadline and a 10 percent late penalty after it. A written request postmarked by January 31 can win an extension to April 15.

  • Individual property: boats, motors, jet skis, mobile homes, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles such as trailers, campers and motorcycles.
  • Business property: machinery, equipment, computers, furniture, fixtures, supplies, farm machinery and race cars.
  • Anyone who owned these on January 1 must list.

If you listed last year, a form arrives by mail. If it does not, getting one is your job. The county gives extensions 7320 or 7321 on 910-671-3060 for individuals and 7319 for business property.

sections.h2: What happens with Robeson County car and truck tax bills?
sections.html:
Tag-related vehicle bills go out every month and come due at the start of the fourth month following a renewal or new tag. A 30-day grace period follows, then 2 percent interest and three-fourths of a percent per month.

Leave it unpaid and the state puts a registration block on the vehicle. Renewal waits until you pay and the collector hands you a MAV-2 form. If you sell a vehicle and surrender the tag to the state, bring the bill of sale and the DMV receipt to the collector, since a refund or prorated bill may be due. A vehicle moved out of North Carolina needs the new state's registration card and the DMV surrender receipt.

sections.h2: How do you contest a Robeson County property value?
sections.html:
Mail your appeal with a postmark earlier than the Board's adjournment. The county says that is usually late April and is advertised before the first meeting. The form comes by written request to the Tax Administrator, addressed to the Administration Center in Lumberton.

The statute behind the board (G.S. 105-322) fixes its first sitting between early April and early May. Still unhappy afterward? The next level up is the state Property Tax Commission, and G.S. 105-290 allows 30 days from the mailed decision to give written notice.

The county suggests supporting papers like a purchase price or damage records. Check the date on your own notice, because the board's calendar is set each year and advertised before it meets. Keep a copy of everything you mail, and use a postmark you can prove.

sections.h2: Which Robeson County tax relief programs can reduce a bill?
sections.html:
North Carolina runs three relief programs, and each owner gets the benefit of only one. Applicants submit Form AV-9 to the county assessor, ideally in January, and the office accepts it up to June 1.

  • Elderly or disabled: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of a home's appraised value comes off, for owners aged 65 or over, or those with a permanent and total disability, under an income cap that the revenue department lists as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value is excluded, and neither age nor income matters. The county's veterans contact, 910-671-3071, assists with the NCDVA-9 certification.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is limited to 4 percent of income at or below the cap and 5 percent between the cap and 150 percent of it ($58,200 for 2026). Anything above is deferred. The application repeats yearly, and five years of ownership and residence come first.

Farm and forest land under present use valuation is a deferment, so if land leaves the program tax on the difference comes due for the current and three prior years plus interest. Property designated historic by local ordinance is taxed at half its appraised value.

sections.h2: What should a Robeson County seller know about tax at closing?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on January 1 is on the hook for that year's tax, so selling in June does not end the seller's exposure. The two sides normally divide the bill by agreement, and the invoice still goes to the seller.

Asking to pay the collector directly at closing removes doubt. If the current bill is not due yet, the office accepts a prepayment using the previous year's rate. Unpaid taxes on a house sold during the year can lead to both names being advertised.

The same office certifies your deed ahead of recording. For the current tax rate, call the office, since no rate is quoted here.

faqs.q: When does a Robeson County tax bill come due?
faqs.a: September 1 is the due date. You can still pay through January 5 without interest, and 2 percent is added starting January 6.

faqs.q: How recent is the Robeson County revaluation?
faqs.a: The latest one is effective January 1, 2024. The eight-year state minimum applies, and the county mentions that commissioners were weighing a shorter four-year cycle.

faqs.q: Who owes the bill when a Robeson house sells in midyear?
faqs.a: Whoever owned it on January 1. The seller therefore receives that year's bill, and closing papers usually prorate the cost.

faqs.q: How do veterans and seniors claim a Robeson County exclusion?
faqs.a: Submit Form AV-9 to the Tax Administration office, plus the NCDVA-9 certificate for a veteran claim. January is the target month, and June 1 is the last day accepted.

faqs.q: When must a Robeson County valuation appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Your appeal needs a postmark before the review board adjourns, which the county says is usually in late April. Write to the Tax Administrator for the form.
